mentl/d57e20c:
Three EXPLICIT allocators per Anchor 0 + Anchor 5: $perm_alloc /
$stage_alloc / $fn_alloc, with NO ambient $current_arena_stage global,
NO if-chain dispatcher, NO drift-1-shape vtable. Each call site chooses
its arena based on the lifetime the caller knows about — Anchor 5
("memory model is a handler swap") made physical AT THE CALL SITE,
not at a dispatcher.

Linear memory partition (32 MiB):
  [1 MiB, 16 MiB)   perm    — long-lived: graph, env, AST, bound Ty/Reason
  [16 MiB, 28 MiB)  stage   — pipeline-stage-local; $stage_reset O(1) free
  [28 MiB, 32 MiB)  fn      — user-fn-local;        $fn_reset    O(1) free

$alloc remains a stable public alias for $perm_alloc — the long-lived
default lifetime contract — so existing graph.wat / env.wat / record.wat /
list.wat / closure.wat / cont.wat call sites stay unchanged. Sites that
know their allocation is transient call $stage_alloc or $fn_alloc
DIRECTLY at the call site; there is no global to set, no boundary
discipline to remember.

$perm_promote(src, size) provides the ownership-transfer primitive at
stage-arena → perm boundaries: when a stage-allocated record earns
long-lived status (e.g., a Ty about to be bound to a graph handle),
caller copies it to perm before next $stage_reset.

Surpass audit (per CLAUDE.md "anything borrowed must surpass"):
  - Refuses C/Rust ambient-allocator drift (mode 5)
  - Refuses dispatcher-as-vtable (mode 1)
  - Refuses string- or int-keyed routing (mode 8)
  - Vocabulary stays arena/region/stage/perm-promote — never
    malloc/free/young-gen/old-gen

mentl/d5c797c:
E1 (W5) · strings via (data ...) segments + arena swap surface.

emit_module runs a collect_string_literals pre-pass over every
LowExpr variant (exhaustive match — no wildcard), assigns each
unique literal a 4-byte-aligned offset starting at 0x10000, and
emits a (data (i32.const <off>) "<escape>") declaration per entry.
Layout per string: 4-byte little-endian length prefix +
\xx-escaped UTF-8 bytes — WAT parser consumes uniformly. The
string_table handler (new, in wasm.ka) carries the entries as
state; set_string_entries seeds once per emit_module; string_offset
resolves each literal at LString emit time. LString now emits a
single (i32.const <offset>) — zero runtime string construction.
The graph knew every literal at compile time (DESIGN Ch 4); emit
projects the layout directly.

emit_memory_arena sibling handler added: same EmitMemory effect,
different global ($arena_ptr), same WAT shape as bump but a
distinct pointer so scope exits can reset in O(1) for arena
semantics. Pipeline can swap ~> emit_memory_bump for
~> emit_memory_arena — same source, different WAT — proving
audit 6's swap surface.

E2 (W6) · record field offsets resolved at lower time.

FieldExpr(rec, field) now lowers to LFieldLoad(handle, lo_rec,
offset_bytes). resolve_field_offset reads rec's type via
lookup_ty, finds the field's index in TRecord(fields) /
TRecordOpen(fields, _) (fields are sorted via field_canonicalize
invariants), computes 4 * index. Backend emits
(i32.load offset=<N>) with the compile-time-resolved offset. All
five backend match sites (collect_fn_names, collect_strings,
emit_fns, emit_let_locals, emit_expr) + lexpr_handle extended for
the new LIR variant. Replaces the broken
